questions.stem: Two parents both show the dominant phenotype, but they have a child with the recessive phenotype. What must be true about both parents?

options.text: They must both be homozygous dominant (BB)

questions.explanation: For a child to show the recessive phenotype (bb), they must receive a recessive allele from each parent. Since both parents show the dominant phenotype, they must each be heterozygous (Bb) carriers of the recessive allele.
